title: block.timestamp drives the two-phase withdrawal window (24h waiting / 48h execution) — load-bearing and intended; miner drift negligible
description: _updateWithdrawalStatus uses block.timestamp for the two-phase window comparisons (>= initiatedAt+WAITING_PERIOD, <= initiatedAt+TOTAL_DURATION, > initiatedAt+TOTAL_DURATION). The 24h/48h windows are far larger than any plausible miner timestamp drift (~12s), so the window cannot be straddled.
impact: None. Timestamp logic is intended and load-bearing; drift is negligible against a 24h/48h window.
likelihood: Not exploitable; timestamp logic is intended and load-bearing.
assumptions: Block timestamps within normal validator drift.
justification: NEW informational/QA. Kept VISIBLE per the static stage's explicit Law-1 policy for a time-driven protocol; drift is negligible against a 24h/48h window. No security impact.
recommendation: No action required; retained as a visible informational note for a time-driven protocol.
